newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Palestinians face off on settlements.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Palestinians face off on settlements.

text.p: The Israeli cabinet convenes on Friday to consider expanding Jewish settlements in occupied Arab land after a Palestinian warning that this would violate their peace deal.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared at the funeral on Thursday of two Jewish settlers killed by Arab gunmen near PLO-ruled Ramallah that he would continue settlement activity.
"When they torture us, we will multiply and break forward," Netanyahu said.
In response, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, speaking in English, told reporters in Gaza: "This is another serious escalation and breaching for what had been agreed upon.
"According to the agreement no one single house (is) to be added to any settlements," he said.

Arafat also condemned the fatal shooting on Thursday of a Palestinian worker by a Jewish farmer who suspected the man was breaking into his house but did not directly condemn the killing of the two Jewish settlers.
"This is a crime against our worker who went to earn a living," Arafat said adding, "We condemn the killing of innocents wherever they are and whoever they are."
Israeli ministers said they would demand at Friday's cabinet meeting that development of Jewish settlements be given priority over other areas in Israel.

Settlement expansion was "a minimal step which was required because of the terrible attack and due to the commitment made by the Netanyahu government to its voters," Transport Minister Yitzhak Levy said, vowing to raise the issue at the meeting.

After taking office in June, Netanyahu lifted a freeze on settlement development imposed by the previous government. More than 130,000 Jewish settlers live among nearly two million Arabs in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

In another move that sparked Arab anger, Israel's Jerusalem municipal planning commission approved a plan earlier in the week to build 132 homes in the heart of Arab East Jerusalem. It now needs ministerial approval to go ahead.
The future of East Jerusalem, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed, is to be determined in final status peace talks which have yet to resume under Netanyahu.
The PLO wants East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future Palestinian state. Israel regards the city as part of its "eternal" capital.

Peace talks between Israel and the PLO have been stalled over a delayed Israeli hand over of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule. Some 400 Jewish settlers live among more than 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron, a flashpoint of violence.
Netanyahu has demanded more security measures be added to the agreement, signed by Israel's previous government, to ensure the settlers' safety. Arafat opposes any changes to the deal.
